about:
RDO Equipment Co. operates a John Deere dealership in Hazen, North Dakota, serving the central region of the state. The location is part of a larger network of RDO Equipment Co. stores, though the founding year and ownership structure of the overall company are not disclosed on this page. The Hazen store is managed by Mike Miller, with Loren Henke handling aftermarket sales.

The dealership sells and services John Deere agriculture equipment, lawn and garden equipment, compact utility tractors, and utility vehicles. It maintains a parts inventory of approximately 650,000 items accessible through an online account system. Service capabilities include machine repair, field technician dispatch, custom hydraulic hose building, precision agriculture technology support, bulk oil and fluid delivery, machine inspections, and after-hours support. Parts can be delivered via route trucks or picked up at drop-off locations.

The company emphasizes a customer-driven approach, stating that its team focuses on building long-term relationships and trust rather than just making sales. It highlights its people as its most valuable asset and offers conveniences such as text alerts for service updates, curbside pickup, and connected equipment monitoring.

about:
REPOWER by Solar Universe Northeast PA operates from Mountain Top, Pennsylvania. The business traces its roots to 1988 when Tony and Susie Delldonna began a home construction company. In 2009 they added solar photovoltaic installation to their services, leveraging decades of building experience to integrate rooftop and ground-mount arrays.

The company provides full-service solar PV installation for residential and commercial customers. Installations range from roof-mounted arrays to ground-mount systems, including retrofits with microinverter technology. The team also provides post-installation monitoring support and warranty service.

Customers include homeowners throughout northeastern Pennsylvania and small businesses seeking to reduce electricity costs. Testimonials reference projects in Jefferson Township and other local communities, with system sizes such as 10.2 kW and 12.06 kW arrays. The company works directly with property owners and coordinates with excavators and utility inspectors.

The Delldonnas emphasize hands-on project management, noting they navigate supply-chain disruptions and bureaucratic hurdles on behalf of clients. Clients cite the firm’s practice of delivering a comprehensive warranty binder, competitive quotes with fixed timelines, and the ability to complete complex retrofits in a single day.

name: RL Hudson
old_description: RL Hudson is a trusted U.S. manufacturer specializing in custom plastic injection molding, rubber components and value-added unit assembly.
about:
RL Hudson was established in 1980 in Tulsa, Oklahoma, initially distributing rubber O-rings to the region's oil industry. The company relocated to Broken Arrow in 2004 and remains under the leadership of the Hudson family, with Rick Hudson as chairman, Jason Hudson as CEO, and Blake Hudson heading sales and marketing.

The company operates as a full-service molder and assembler, running plastic injection presses from 85 to 4,000 tons with scientific (decoupled) molding monitored by AuthenTIG systems. It also produces custom rubber parts via injection, transfer, and compression molding, plus wrapped and extruded formed hoses. In-house tooling design, machining, and maintenance support both molding lines, while plastic welding (ultrasonic, spin, hot-plate, vibration), pad printing, and a high-volume automated assembly line round out the operation.

Customers rely on the firm for part consolidation, metal-to-plastic conversions, and end-to-end assembly of multi-component units.

The company emphasizes its integrated "under one roof" model—combining molding, rubber, welding, tooling, and assembly—to deliver tighter quality control, faster turnaround, and cost-effective solutions.

name: RW Collective
about:
RW Collective is headquartered in Rockford, Alabama, and operates a flagship showroom at 156 S. Main Street in High Point, North Carolina. The company was co-founded by Michael Carey and Rebekah Osborn, whose backgrounds in law enforcement and global manufacturing, respectively, shaped a platform built to connect people, product, and purpose. Carey, also owner of Atelier Home, serves as CEO, while Osborn, owner of Beyond Borders Furniture Co., serves as COO.

The company functions as a to-the-trade furniture line, offering a curated portfolio that includes handcrafted hardwoods and USA-made custom upholstery under the RW Custom Classics label. The custom upholstery program provides more than 300 fabric options with a standard lead time of four to six weeks. Wholesale partners receive tiered pricing, flexible ordering, and dedicated support with swatches and inventory updates.

RW Collective sells exclusively to retailers, interior designers, and industry professionals through its wholesale program. Its products are described as battle-tested in retail and design environments, and the company maintains year-round showrooms in major markets to serve those partners. The lineup spans living, dining, bedroom, and occasional furniture, including game tables designed for mahjong and cards.

The founders positioned the business around operational clarity and creative curation, aiming to deliver breadth, flexibility, and streamlined solutions that help dealers and designers sell more effectively. The emphasis on systems that work—from product development to logistics—reflects Carey’s operational background, while the aesthetic direction reflects Osborn’s global design perspective.

old_description: Race Tech Race Cars and Components is a leading manufacturer of fine racing machines.
about:
Race Tech Race Cars and Components, Inc. was founded in 1988 in Burlington, North Carolina, by champion driver and builder Russ Farmer, who remains president and CEO. The company began as a specialist builder of custom race cars and has grown into a full-service operation for drag racing competitors.

The shop produces custom-built dragsters, roadsters, and doorslammers, each designed in CAD to individual specifications. In-house capabilities include chassis and body fabrication, MIG/TIG welding, tube bending, CNC plasma cutting on a 4-by-8-foot table, and finishing services such as powder coating, polishing, chroming, and custom painting. The company also assembles AN braided stainless hoses as an authorized Goodridge distributor and offers nitrous bottle refills.

Race Tech serves drag racing teams across the NHRA Sportsman ranks and bracket-racing enthusiasts.

The company emphasizes reliability and ease of maintenance, citing design features such as removable crossmembers for transmission access, master cylinders mounted outside the driver compartment, and optimized driveline angles. Farmer notes that the parts division aims to match or beat warehouse pricing while providing technical expertise.

old_description: Radcliff Wire routinely works with over 60 different metals to expertly produce standard and custom wire in a broad variety of shapes, sizes, and finishes.
about:
Radcliff Wire, Inc. operates from Bristol, Connecticut, in the heart of the Eastern U.S. spring industry. The company was founded over six decades ago to supply spring manufacturers with hard-to-locate flat and shaped wire, and has since grown into a global supplier of custom wire products.

The company produces flat, square, and special shaped wire in more than 60 metals and alloys, managing every step from raw material certification through final delivery. Its in-house capabilities include wire drawing, shaping, and a full suite of testing equipment such as Rockwell hardness testers, tensile testers, laser micrometers, optical comparators, and metallurgical microscopy.

Radcliff Wire serves aerospace, electronics, medical, automotive, and consumer product industries, providing wire that meets exacting standards for each sector. The company also supplies DFARS-compliant material for defense applications and maintains REACH and RoHS compliance for European markets.

Quality differentiation comes from an ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system, a workforce averaging 15 years of wire-industry experience, and a structured cross-training program that ensures consistent competence across all positions.

name: Radiance Technologies
old_description: Our employee-owners can be trusted and they trust their teammates to do the “right thing”
about:
Founded in 1999 in Huntsville, Alabama, by George Clark, John Dennis, and Scott Dublin, Radiance Technologies began as an employee-owned subcontractor supporting the U.S. Army Space and Missile Defense Command. The company later relocated its corporate headquarters to Ruston, Louisiana.

Radiance delivers intelligence analysis, cyber operations, directed energy systems, hypersonics, space solutions, and AI/ML applications for defense and intelligence customers. Its capabilities span systems engineering, modeling and simulation, software development, prototyping, low-rate manufacturing, and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The firm operates facilities in nine states and project offices in fourteen states, employing over 500 people as of 2015 with revenue of $116.7 million that year.

Primary customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, the Intelligence Community, the U.S. Army (SMDC, INSCOM), NASA, and commercial aerospace firms. The company has supported Army hypersonic missile programs, high-energy laser development, and space-based communication and ISR missions.

The founders structured Radiance as an employee-owned enterprise to align incentives with mission success, emphasizing a culture that tackles problems others deem impossible. Leadership states that this ownership model keeps the focus on delivering game-changing solutions rather than maximizing short-term profit.

name: Raeed & Sons
old_description: Mon–Thu 10am–6pm · Fri 12–6pm · Walk-ins welcome at 1105 S 12th St
about:
Raeed & Sons opened its doors in May 2013 at 1105 South 12th Street in Bismarck, North Dakota. The shop is family‑owned and operated by Raeed Douri, who brought over thirty years of electronics experience to the venture. He started the business with a simple mission: give every broken device a fair shot and treat every customer like family.

The shop provides component‑level repair for a wide range of electronics. Services include screen, battery, and charge‑port replacement on smartphones and tablets; hardware upgrades, custom builds, virus removal, and full diagnostics on Windows and Mac computers; and board‑level work on engine control units, transmission modules, power supplies, and industrial PCBs — covering capacitor replacement, IC reflow, and trace repair. Free diagnostics are standard, and most repairs are completed in under an hour. The operation runs as a walk‑in service center with no appointment needed.

Customers span individual consumers with damaged phones or laptops, automotive shops needing ECU or module repair, and industrial clients with faulty control boards or power supplies. The shop’s expertise in component‑level fixes often saves customers the cost of full unit replacement, a value highlighted by automotive and industrial referrals.

Raeed & Sons emphasizes personal attention, transparent pricing, and a no‑pressure approach. The company cites its A+ Better Business Bureau rating, 100% recommendation rate on Facebook, and a track record of thousands of repairs as evidence of its commitment to sending every customer home happier than they arrived.

Rainier Woodworking Co operates from Tacoma, Washington, where it has served the Greater Puget Sound region for many years. The company focuses on producing heirloom-quality cabinetry using locally sourced wood, emphasizing respect for the material and long-lasting craftsmanship.

The shop manufactures a full line of cabinetry, offering custom design services that translate client visions into finished pieces. Production includes woodworking, finishing, and assembly, with a proprietary project-tracking app (RW CabTracker) available on the Apple App Store to keep customers informed throughout the process.

Rainier’s cabinetry is distributed exclusively through professional designers and established kitchen and bath dealers along the West Coast. This channel-focused approach means the company works closely with design professionals and showroom partners rather than selling direct to end users.

The business stresses fair pricing and adherence to client budgets and timelines, positioning its locally made, wood-centric products as a durable alternative to mass-market options. A stated commitment to tree stewardship underpins the material selection and build quality.

Ramco Automotive, founded in 2007 and centrally located in Miami, Florida, was established by founders drawing on 40 years of industry experience. The company began as an independent manufacturer and distributor of electrical and electronic replacement parts for motor vehicles, targeting the automotive aftermarket.

The company manufactures a full line of sensors and vehicle parts under the RAMCO brand, including crankshaft position sensors, idle air control valves, camshaft position sensors, fuel pressure regulators, coolant temperature sensors, ignition control modules, ignition coils, and knock detonation sensors. It also distributes products from other aftermarket manufacturers through an online platform that supports ACES and PIES data standards, enabling dynamic catalog management and cross-referencing capabilities.

Ramco serves distributors and retailers across the automotive aftermarket, with a growing focus on original equipment and original equipment service channels. Its customer base spans the United States, Latin America, Europe, and the Middle East, supported by express international shipping to over 50 countries.

The company emphasizes honesty, quality guaranteed, reliability, and timeliness in order delivery as core values.

name: Ramtel Corporation
old_description: Ramtel specializes in Custom Silk Screened phone panels, individualized to your needs
about:
Ramtel Corporation, based in Johnston, Rhode Island, traces its origins to 1983 when the company (then called Ramtech) was formed following the divestiture of the telephone industry. The venture began as a collaboration with an Ivy League university in New England to address the vulnerability of standard receiver phones to vandalism.

Today Ramtel manufactures a range of security communication devices, including custom silk‑screened phone panels, hands‑free emergency phones, elevator phones, and VoIP endpoints. Production encompasses silk screening on anodized aluminum, fabrication of non‑rusting stainless‑steel columns and enclosures, electronics assembly with conformal coating, and weather‑ and vandal‑resistant finishing. All assembly and testing occur in‑house at the Rhode Island facility, with multiple quality‑assurance checkpoints throughout the build process.

Ramtel distinguishes itself as the only U.S. manufacturer that fabricates stainless‑steel columns in‑house and offers fully customized silk‑screened panels for each project. The company emphasizes made‑in‑USA production, a service‑first approach, and a history of introducing new features — such as piezo switches, ADA‑compliant indicator lights, and remote diagnostics — ahead of the market.

about:
Ready Made Plastic Trays was founded in 1990 in Meridian, Idaho, and has operated as a domestic manufacturer of thermoformed plastic trays for over three decades. The company emphasizes American-made production and domestically sourced materials traceable to their original manufacturers.

The company produces stock and custom thermoformed trays for packaging and storage, offering pocket shapes including square, round, and rectangular configurations with a maximum depth of two inches. An on-site CNC tooling shop enables custom fixture design and re-tooling for specific client requirements. Standard materials include High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS), with food-grade, medical-grade, and anti-static variants available.

Ready Made serves industries such as aerospace, automotive, dental, electronics, firearms, food and beverage, machining, manufacturing, medical, and optical. Customers range from medical device manufacturers and mechanical shops to aerospace suppliers and food processors, as well as distributors and individual buyers seeking protective packaging for shipping delicate or complex components.

The company positions itself as a service-first partner, highlighting rapid production, no-nonsense ordering, free samples, volume discounts, and direct access to a real person for support. Its ISO 9001:2015 certification underpins a commitment to meeting customer and supplier needs while maintaining inventory levels for quick turnaround.

Clients range from homeowners seeking dining tables, coffee tables, and end tables to businesses outfitting offices, restaurants, and bars. name: Remcon Plastics
old_description: Since 1982 • Family Owned • Built to Perform • Rotomolded in the USA • Traffic Safety • Material Handling • Custom OEM Solutions • Serious Capacity • Real Relationships
about:
Remcon Plastics was founded in November 1982 by Peter and Doren Connors in Pennsylvania. The venture was backed by the Remmey and Connors families — Doren's parents Bill and Nancy Remmey and Pete's mother Lorraine Connors — whose savings and names (Remcon = Remmey + Connors) launched the business. The founders believed a small, family-owned rotational molder could compete with larger firms by building more durable products and standing behind them. In 1990, after eight years in Conshohocken, the operation moved to Reading, Pennsylvania, tripling plant size.

Today, Remcon runs a 75,000-square-foot facility in Reading with eight rotational molding machines. It produces material handling containers, MASH-compliant water-filled traffic barricades and longitudinal channelizers, and custom OEM rotationally molded components. Automation and advanced production systems increase capacity and consistency, and the company also works with production partners who share its engineering and quality standards.

Remcon serves traffic safety, material handling, and custom OEM markets. Its traffic safety line includes the Guardsafe 36 barricade and other MASH-compliant channelizers used on jobsites nationwide. One original OEM customer from the early 1980s remains a partner today.

The company's differentiation traces to its founding principles: durability over shortcuts, thoughtful design to prevent field failures, and integrity in every decision. Pete Connors, still active as president, engineered the "R" lip and replaceable pallet system that extended bin life from months to over a decade, reshaping industry expectations. Leadership has transitioned to the next generation — Tracy Connors as CEO and James Connors as Director of Design — while maintaining the family-owned structure and the original commitment to standing behind every product shipped.

name: Resonant Link Medical: Wireless Technology for Next-Generation Implantables
old_description: Make power an asset, not a hurdle, to your medical device with the fastest and most patient-friendly wireless power and charging for bioelectronics.
about:
Resonant Link Medical was founded in 2017 in Burlington, Vermont, by Aaron Stein, who serves as chief technology officer. The company emerged from Stein's postdoctoral research at Dartmouth College, where he pioneered advances in resonant coils and power electronics that enabled new levels of efficiency and range for wireless power transfer.

The company develops the Aurion WPT™ wireless power and data platform, which uses inductive coupling to recharge or continuously power implantable medical devices through the skin without transcutaneous leads. Its product platforms include Eterni™ for millimeter-scale implants (up to 500 mW continuous power), Vivigo™ Fast Charger (20-minute recharge over a large range), and Cardessa™ High Power Platform (10–15 W driveline-free power). Resonant Link also provides feasibility studies and regulatory-ready testing and integration services. To date, the team has designed wireless power solutions for more than 50 implantable device types.

Customers span neuromodulation, cardiac rhythm management, sensing and diagnostics, circulatory assist, cranial and brain-computer interfaces, sleep apnea, implantable drug delivery, urinary and gastrointestinal, and smart orthopedics. Partners include Paradromics, which used the technology to maintain power through thick tissue layers for a brain-computer interface, and Resonetics, which collaborated on next-generation bioelectronic devices. One brain-computer interface company reached human studies within 15 months of development start.

Resonant Link says its mission is to enable smaller, smarter, and longer-lasting implants that help people get well and stay well. The company emphasizes that its platform delivers 10× faster charging than conventional wireless at double the range, allows implants as small as 3 mm, and maintains uninterrupted power and data transfer during patient movement—all while reducing development risk through regulatory-ready processes.

Restoration & Performance Motorcars operates from a red barn on Monkton Road in Vergennes, Vermont. The business traces its roots to 1986 when Peter Markowski, a Vermont native who had spent two decades restoring a Ferrari Barchetta to its original specification, built the shop to turn his passion for classic European sports cars into a full-time venture. Markowski, the oldest of eight children from a dairy farm, had previously worked in construction, banking, and heavy-truck sales before founding the company.

The shop provides restoration, sales, and maintenance services for classic European sports cars, with a focus on Ferrari and Porsche models.

The company emphasizes craftsmanship and originality as its guiding principles, a standard Markowski established during his early restoration work. After nearly four decades of family ownership, the business was sold in September 2024 to four longtime employees—Nate Barcomb, Rolf Humburg, Keith Carnevale, and Jennifer Valz—who continue the operation with Markowski remaining involved.

The company designs and installs custom solar systems for recreational vehicles and off-grid properties. Services include system design, installation, consultations, and detailed quotes. Each project is tailored to the customer's specific goals and budget, with an emphasis on safety and reliability. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

Primary customers are RV owners seeking mobile power freedom, owners of remote cabins or off-grid homes, and homeowners looking to reduce utility dependence. The company serves the RV/mobile market, off-grid residential sector, and broader renewable energy space, with concrete examples including Harvest Hosts and Boondockers Welcome overnight stays, cabin generator replacement, and whole-home off-grid conversions.

The business was born from firsthand experience: the founders wanted to run appliances silently while boondocking, keep food cold without generator noise, and maximize time away from hookups. That personal need drives their approach — they build systems they would trust for their own family's comfort and independence.

old_description: Founded on 30+ years of expertise in textile fabrication, sourcing and product design, Rival Technologies exists to streamline complex development cycles and deliver exceptional results, globally.
about:
Rival Technologies, LLC is headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. The company was founded on over three decades of expertise in textile fabrication, sourcing, and product design, aiming to streamline complex development cycles and deliver exceptional results globally. While a specific founding year is not disclosed, the business traces its roots to 30-plus years of industry experience. Gerry Van Wagner serves as CEO.

The company provides high-quality sewn products and comprehensive textile fabrication services. Its core processes include cut-and-sew manufacturing, thermoforming of hard-shell components, strap fabrication, anti-migration and silicone engineering, and supply of performance fabrics. Rival operates facilities in the United States, Vietnam, and China, enabling scalable, cost-effective production. The team is described as lean and capable, supporting rapid prototyping and an engineering-led phase-gate methodology that manages product development from concept through commercialization.

Rival serves sectors such as healthcare, safety, military, and law enforcement, with a particular focus on medical and orthopedic soft goods. Its customers include U.S. brands and global manufacturers that require durable, mission-critical sewn and thermoformed products. The company emphasizes long-term partnerships and supply-chain reliability for clients in critical markets.

Rival differentiates itself through its U.S.-based headquarters, which provides real-time communication and fast decision-making, combined with global manufacturing reach. Its in-house design and development capabilities, on-site prototyping, strategic sourcing, and deep supplier relationships are intended to reduce risk, accelerate speed to market, and ensure quality outcomes. The company was built to move fast, think smart, and go global without losing sight of detail.

about:
Riverpoint Medical originated in Portland, Oregon, as a family-run business focused on surgical sutures for the medical and animal markets. The company does not disclose its founding year, but its history describes a trajectory from a small suture supplier to a vertically integrated medical device manufacturer with a new production facility in Costa Rica.

Today the company designs, develops, and manufactures implantable textiles and fibers, including orthopedic implants, high-strength fiber solutions, cordless LED surgical headlights, and brachytherapy devices for oncology. Its in-house capabilities span custom braiding, precision needle fabrication, suture material expertise, product concept development, regulatory support, prototyping, testing, validation, finished device assembly, packaging, sterilization, and private labeling. The firm emphasizes a vertically integrated model that covers design, manufacturing, and branding under one roof.

Riverpoint serves the orthopedic, veterinary, dental, sports medicine, and oncology markets, working with medical device companies that need end-to-end product realization. Customers range from startups seeking prototyping and regulatory guidance to established firms requiring volume production and private-label packaging.

The company cites its quality system—compliant with FDA Quality System Regulations and ISO 13485—as a core differentiator, along with a mission to rapidly innovate high-quality devices that improve patient outcomes. A dedicated marketing team provides packaging design and branding support to accelerate time to market.

about:
Riverside Sheet Metal & Contracting operates from Medford, Massachusetts, where it has been providing custom architectural metal fabrication for over three decades.

The shop fabricates a wide range of architectural metal products, including standing-seam metal roofing, copper and aluminum gutters and downspouts, chimney caps, cupolas, finials, flashing, and interior items such as copper, stainless steel, and zinc counter tops, backsplashes, and hood vents. In-house capabilities cover cutting, bending (with brakes and shears rated for 13-foot-2-inch lengths), forming, welding, soldering, plasma cutting, and panel curving. The company also fields installation crews that handle roofing, gutter, and accessory mounting on site.

Riverside serves the roofing and construction industries, supplying both contractors and homeowners. Its portfolio spans residential projects — custom gutters, chimney shrouds, and kitchen counter tops — as well as commercial work for restaurants and coffee shops that specify copper bar tops, zinc island tops, and outdoor counter tops. The firm also provides roofing supply and related sheet metal products to trade customers.

The company emphasizes that fabricating the products it installs allows it to control costs and quality, a point highlighted in its own messaging. Membership in the North East Roofing Contractors Association and the National Roofing Contractors Association, along with Massachusetts licensing (HIC #159489, CSL #CS40485), underscores its commitment to industry standards.

about:
Robco Steel Fabricators is based in Wells River, Vermont. Founded in 1985 by brothers Bill and Bob Rowden, the company originated from their family’s multi‑generational dairy operation, Rowden’s Dairy. Recognizing a local need for construction and maintenance of feed mills, they converted the dairy business into a steel fabrication shop, naming it Robco as an abbreviation of Rowden Bros. Corp.

The shop also performs on‑site welding and installation. Through sister companies Rowden Crane & Rigging and New England Millwrights, Robco extends its offering to include crane and rigging services, trucking, and millwright work, creating a single source for design, fabrication, and installation.

Projects range from farm feed‑mill construction to commercial handrail systems and industrial structural steel. Robco delivers within a 100‑mile radius of Wells River.

Robco emphasizes compliance with OSHA regulations at its shop and on job sites, and follows ADA guidelines for applicable projects. The founders’ original goal — providing a local, service‑oriented fabrication and installation resource — remains the guiding principle.

about:
Roberto's Sofa Factory operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has served the Arizona Valley for decades. The business began in a garage when Roberto, an immigrant from Mexico, founded a small family-owned upholstery shop driven by a passion for craftsmanship. Today, the company remains family-owned and operated, with Roberto's sons, brother, and grandchildren working alongside each other in the shop.

The shop provides a full range of upholstery services, including custom cushion design and creation, sofa and couch reupholstery, chair and recliner upholstery, sectional reupholstery, frame repair and reinforcement, spring replacement, leather upholstery and repair, mid-century modern and antique furniture restoration, pattern matching, foam cutting and replacement, stitching and seam repair, zipper repair, and decorative trims such as piping, tufting, and nailheads. The team also handles commercial projects for hotels, restaurants, and offices, and offers weather‑resistant fabrics for outdoor furniture. Work follows a four‑step process: consultation and design planning, furniture preparation, upholstery and detailing, and final inspection with delivery or pickup.

Clients range from residential homeowners seeking to restore a favorite piece to businesses in the hospitality and corporate sectors needing contract‑grade upholstery. The company serves all of Arizona, with recent projects spanning private homes, restaurants, offices, and hotels.

Roberto's Sofa Factory distinguishes itself by educating customers at every stage, emphasizing transparency about timelines, costs, and materials. The family legacy centers on treating each piece as if it were their own and each customer like family, a philosophy that has generated word‑of‑mouth referrals and repeat business over decades.

old_description: Robling excels in Design for Manufacturing and Assembly, prototyping and benchtop performance characterization, with an early focus on material, tooling, and manufacturing process selection.
about:
Robling Medical, LLC operates from Youngsville, North Carolina, where it has accumulated over 35 years of medical device manufacturing experience. The company focuses exclusively on medical devices, with more than 75 percent of its work in interventional and minimally invasive surgical applications.

As a full-service contract manufacturer, Robling handles design for manufacturing and assembly, prototyping, and benchtop performance characterization, with early emphasis on material, tooling, and process selection. Its capabilities span sterile disposable manufacturing — including bonding, tipping, heat sealing, ultrasonic welding, and kitting — as well as electro-mechanical assembly, box builds, cable and harness assembly, PC board flashing, and functional testing. The firm also provides vertically integrated packaging services, running high-speed Multivac lines with inline printing on Tyvek 1073B, paper, and poly film, and manages contract sterilization via ethylene oxide, gamma, and electron beam. Annual output exceeds 10 million sterile devices, from prototype runs to full-scale production.

Robling serves medical device and life sciences OEMs across a broad range of clinical markets: women’s health, urology, fluid management, cardiology, orthopedics, neurology, oncology, gastrointestinal, ENT, vascular, and respiratory. Customers include large, mid-sized, and newly commercialized MedTech original equipment manufacturers.

The company differentiates itself through cross-market experience that it says yields proven processes, faster ramp-up, and fewer surprises. Its quality system is described as flexible and collaborative, offering clients the option to use Robling’s QMS or work within their own. Quality certifications include MDD 93/42/EEC, Japan PMDA Foreign Manufacturer Accreditation, Brazil ANVISA certification, compliance with SOR/92-282, and Korean GMP compliance.

The business positions itself between national broadline distributors and conventional retail chains, aiming to serve both commercial foodservice operators and retail shoppers in the mid-coast Maine region.

name: Rockledge Farm Woodworks
old_description: Unlocking the beauty of Vermont Hardwoods, For Those Seeking the Road Less Traveled
about:
Rockledge Farm Woodworks operates from a 200-year-old hill farm in Reading, Vermont, where a family-owned woodworking tradition spans four generations. The business traces its roots to a mail-order venture that sold wooden furniture from the farm, and today the converted barns house workshops, a gallery, and offices for the small, family-operated company.

The workshop produces custom furniture and one-of-a-kind pieces crafted from sustainably harvested Vermont hardwoods such as birdseye maple, curly maple, black walnut, cherry, flame birch, and various burls. Each project begins with hand-selected lumber sourced from small local mills, and the team builds everything from heirloom tables and chairs to accessories including cutting boards, bowls, utensils, jewelry boxes, game boards, and bentwood oval ware. No two pieces are identical; the firm describes its output as “one-of-a-kind, one-at-a-time” handcrafted work.

Customers include private clients who collaborate on custom designs as well as select galleries and stores across the country that carry the accessory line. The company does not operate as a production shop with a fixed catalog; instead, it treats every commission as a fresh start, developing designs directly with the buyer.

The founders’ philosophy centers on letting the wood itself guide the design—unusual live-edge slabs may sit for years until the “proper use becomes apparent”—and on keeping the supply chain local unless a specific material cannot be found in Vermont. This approach, they say, distinguishes them from volume-oriented furniture makers.

Rohrer Corporation, headquartered in Warwick, Rhode Island, operates nine manufacturing facilities across the United States and Mexico. Rohrer's ezCombo® and ecoCombo® programs target brand owners seeking sustainable, cost-effective packaging with rapid turnaround.

Rohrer differentiates itself through its ezCombo® program, which promises speed, quality, and value, and its ecoCombo® program, described as the packaging industry's first post-consumer recycled materials combo offering. about:
Sapphire Systems Inc. was incorporated in 2007 by Charles Allmon and John Outwater in a garage laboratory to commercialize crystal-growth innovations. The company soon moved to a larger facility in Bedford, Massachusetts, along the Route 128 corridor northwest of Boston, to develop larger systems and begin commercial production.

The company grows optical-quality sapphire plates using the Edge-defined, Film-fed Growth (EFG) method, which it considers ideal for large-area plates. Current production yields plates 15‑5/8 inches wide, with standard plates of 30 by 15‑5/8 inches by 3/8 inch thick planned for pilot production; larger plates are available on request. Sapphire Systems has also produced and sold optical sapphire fiber and sapphire ribbon for superconductor substrates.

Its customers span military and commercial markets. For defense, the firm supplies sensor windows, transparent armor, and bullet‑proof windows used on range finders, infrared cameras, and personnel protection systems. In semiconductor manufacturing, its sapphire components serve as windows, wafer carriers, and other hardware that withstand corrosive chip‑fabrication environments.

Sapphire Systems differentiates itself through its patented EFG growth technology and the scale of its plates, which it describes as among the largest commercially available. The company holds three U.S. patents, an R&D 100 Award, and an SBIR Award for its superconducting wire epitaxial growth process.

name: Sasquatch Water Company, LLC
old_description: Providing Central Oregon with safe, clean 12 step Reverse Osmosis filtered and Alkaline drinking water at an affordable price.
about:
Sasquatch Water Company, LLC operates from Redmond, Oregon, delivering purified alkaline drinking water and bagged ice to customers throughout Central Oregon. The company also designs and builds the Diamond Skid, an industrial-grade reverse osmosis system sold in domestic and international markets.

The core service is a 12-step reverse osmosis filtration process that employs more than 50 individual filters to produce alkaline water with a pH of 8.8. The process includes pre-filtration down to 20 microns, carbon filtration, a 5-micron pre-filter, a high-pressure stainless steel RO pump, a .0002-micron membrane, UV sterilization, and optional ozone treatment. Water is stored in FDA-approved tanks and repressurized for consistent delivery. In addition to water, the company produces two styles of bagged ice: Cristal Clear half-dome and nugget ice. On the equipment side, the Diamond Skid line features a powder-coated steel frame, prewired electrical panel, stainless steel booster pump, and components that carry NSF, FDA, UL, or ETL approvals. Models share a common footprint of 90″L × 30″W × 74″H and can be customized with feed pumps, TDS meters, water softeners, and chemical injection.

Residential and commercial customers in Central Oregon subscribe to 24/7 water delivery, while the Diamond Skid systems serve domestic and international buyers needing turnkey water purification for bottling, vending, or industrial processes.

Sasquatch Water emphasizes purity and affordability, citing independent lab certification of its water and a filtration train designed to remove 99.9% of impurities from source, plumbing, and municipal lines. The Diamond Skid was developed to answer the call for pure, quality, consumable drinking water in varied feed-water conditions, with recovery rates up to 60% and salt rejection of 90–98%.

The customer base is primarily residential, drawing from Roanoke and the surrounding Central Illinois region, with a broader reach across the Midwest. The company emphasizes its role as a community fixture, serving neighbors and friends through a team that includes in-house designers, delivery and installation crews, and customer relations specialists.

The Sauder family positions the business on a tradition of personal service that spans generations. Wade Sauder describes great customer service not just as a tradition but as a way of life, while Jeff Sauder highlights trust, relationships, and making every customer feel like part of the family. old_description: Need thousands of parts laser cut, bent, and powder coated under one roof? Savant Mfg is the place for you.
about:
Savant Manufacturing Inc. is based in Kinder, Louisiana. The company traces its roots to 1978 when founder Kevin Savant, then 14, built his first four-wheeler rack in his backyard using homemade tools and scrap metal. After years of part-time orders, the business was formalized in 1985 with a workshop on Highway 383 in Kinder, starting with one employee. The company remains a self-made, founder-owned operation.

SMI operates as a full-service metal fabrication and machine shop, offering laser cutting (including a 6 kW fiber laser), CNC bending (press brakes up to 12 feet wide), CNC milling and turning (Haas equipment), turret punching (two machines), plasma cutting, robotic welding, powder coating (automated line accommodating parts up to 60 inches wide), sanding, deburring, and PEM hardware insertion. The shop also provides engineering and design support using SolidWorks and AutoCAD, and maintains a FARO Arm CMM for inspection. They handle prototype through production volumes, with the capacity to produce thousands of parts under one roof.

The company originally specialized in ATV and UTV accessories—front and rear racks, drop racks, floor boards, gun racks, stick shifts, and similar items—custom-fitted to new models each year. Today, SMI serves a broader range of clients as a job shop, manufacturing, modifying, and repairing prototype and production parts for various industries across the southern United States, leveraging a network of partner shops for processes not performed in-house.

SMI emphasizes a quality system built on hiring for attitude, quality, cooperation, and growth, with quarterly employee reviews and multi-stage inspections (welders, buffers, painters, packers, shippers). The founder’s early experience shaped a culture of double-checking every weld and finish, and the automated powder-coat line ensures consistent, durable finishes. The company states its differentiator is a precise mix of quality, service, delivery, and price, staying on the cutting edge of manufacturing technology.

about:
Sawyer Made operates from East Calais, Vermont. The company was formally launched in 2012 by George Sawyer, building on a chairmaking lineage that began in 1982 when his father, Dave Sawyer, an MIT-trained mechanical engineer, built his first Windsor chair. Dave spent three decades refining Windsor and Shaker designs, teaching hundreds of students at his Vermont studio, and placing pieces in the Boston Museum of Fine Arts. George, who grew up in the Woodbury shop, studied industrial design at RISD and worked in product design and architecture before returning to Vermont to establish Sawyer Made as a family-owned workshop.

The workshop produces custom chairs and benches that reinterpret American Windsor and Shaker traditions through traditional green‑woodworking techniques and hand‑cut joinery. Each piece is made to order using sustainably sourced wood, with an emphasis on ethical production and enduring aesthetics. Output is limited to small‑batch, made‑to‑measure seating rather than volume runs; no facility size or headcount figures are published.

The brand has also been featured in design publications such as The New York Times Style Magazine, Domino, Metropolis, and Fine Woodworking, indicating a following among design professionals and collectors.

The founders frame the venture as a re‑envisioning of seating craftsmanship — combining Dave’s technical mastery of Windsor geometry with George’s industrial‑design perspective to create pieces that are “handmade, sustainable, ethically produced, and beautiful.” The business was started to carry forward a living tradition of green woodworking while adapting it for contemporary homes.

Schluter's Metal Artwork and Welding operates from Helena, Montana, where it was founded in 2011 by Colton Schluter, a journeyman-carded welder. The company provides custom metal fabrication and welding — railings, gates, stairs, structural steel, furniture, and decorative pieces such as wildlife silhouettes, wall art, and custom signs — all cut, bent, and welded in-house from steel, aluminum, and stainless. An on-site powder coating line, operated under the PowderCoating of Helena banner, offers more than 6,500 colors with gloss, matte, texture, and heat-resistant finishes. The shop also coats customer-supplied parts, handling everything from automotive wheels and roll cages to commercial brackets and handrails. To date, the team has completed over 1,000 projects.

Schluter's serves homeowners, contractors, and commercial builders throughout the Helena area and Lewis & Clark County. Residential clients commission handrails, gates, and artistic metalwork; commercial contractors rely on the shop for structural steel elements, bollards, and brackets. Other fabrication shops without in-house coating send their work to Schluter's for finishing, and automotive customers bring parts for durable powder coating.

The business emphasizes direct, end-to-end control: every project is custom with no catalog parts, the same shop that fabricates a piece also coats it, and owner Colton Schluter oversees design, fit-up, and finish personally. Quotes are firm, with scope changes discussed before any extra cost.

name: Seaside Casual Furniture
old_description: Having trouble locating the right Seaside Casual product, service or showroom?
about:
Seaside Casual Furniture operates from Coventry, Rhode Island, where the brand was officially established in 1996. Its roots trace back to 1911 when Carold "Kit" Arnold opened the Arnold Lumber Company, a sawmill that evolved into a multi-generational family business. In the 1990s, "Art" Arnold Jr. began selling handcrafted mahogany Adirondack chairs from the lumber company's door shop, turning a hobby into a dedicated furniture line. The company was acquired in 2025 by The Prestwick Companies, a family-owned, Made-in-USA furnishings group based in Sussex, Wisconsin, with manufacturing remaining in Rhode Island.

The company engineers and manufactures luxury outdoor furniture using its proprietary EnviroWood, a non-porous, UV-stabilized recycled HDPE (also called Marine Grade Polymer) developed in 1999 to withstand coastal New England conditions. The product range spans over 400 SKUs, including Adirondack chairs, deep seating, dining and bar sets, fire tables, and planters. All pieces are built at the Rhode Island facility, and the company offers complimentary design services that provide layout planning, finish selection, and 3D renderings before production.

Seaside Casual serves residential homeowners, hospitality operators at high-end resorts and private estates, and commercial projects through a dealer network. Its furniture is specified for environments that demand resistance to salt spray, chlorine, oils, and extreme weather, with substantial weight to stay grounded in high winds.

The brand differentiates itself through a zero-maintenance material that runs UV-inhibited pigment through the entire profile, ensuring color retention for decades. The 1999 material innovation was driven by the need for furniture that could endure corrosive sea air, harsh winters, and relentless sun without sanding, oiling, or covering.

Sensitron Semiconductor operates from Deer Park, New York, drawing on over 50 years of heritage in high-reliability power electronics. The company's founding year and original owners are not disclosed in public materials, but it has established itself as a specialist in solid-state power management for demanding markets.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of power electronic components, including high-power rectifier bridges, lightweight SiC and IGBT power modules, motor controllers, solid-state power controllers, and a full line of JANS QPL diodes and transistors. Its capabilities span custom design, hybrid microelectronics, chip-on-board packaging, power conversion assemblies, and screening and test services such as up-screening commercial discrete parts to military standards. Specific part numbers referenced include the SCP-5282 series TVS modules, SPM1 Series SiC power modules, and SEPD Series solid-state relay power controllers.

Sensitron serves commercial aerospace, space and launch vehicles, defense (aerospace, vehicle, naval, missiles), medical, and high-reliability industrial applications. Its rotating rectifier assemblies are used in aerospace and defense generators rated up to 1000V, 120A, and 27,500 RPM, while its SuperClamp TVS devices protect 115Vac and 270Vdc systems against lightning and voltage spikes per MIL-STD-704, MIL-STD-1399, and DO-160.

The company emphasizes its certifications to MIL-PRF-38534 Class K for hybrid microelectronics and MIL-PRF-19500 for JANS-level discrete diodes, along with AS9100 registration. It highlights patented packaging technology such as the High Strength SMD package, which improves temperature and power cycling performance, and ultralight SiC power bridge modules that deliver high power in a small footprint.

about:
SkyWater Technology is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota. The company was formed in 2017 when it acquired the Bloomington fabrication facility originally established by Cypress Semiconductor in 1991. SkyWater operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of IonQ and is described as the largest exclusively U.S.-based semiconductor foundry with no foreign controlling interest.

The company provides semiconductor foundry services including wafer manufacturing, advanced packaging, and technology development across three U.S. facilities. Its flagship Bloomington fab offers 91,000 square feet of Class 10 cleanroom space with 200 mm equipment supporting 90 nm and larger geometries. The Kissimmee, Florida facility adds 36,000 square feet of Class 1,000 and 10,000 cleanroom space with 200/300 mm equipment for advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration. The Austin, Texas fab (acquired in 2025) provides 114,000 square feet of Class 1 cleanroom, 30,000 square feet of probe and test area, and 200 mm equipment capable of 65 nm geometries. SkyWater’s process portfolio spans CMOS, MEMS, photonics, superconducting devices, rad-hard technologies, and read-out integrated circuits (ROICs).

SkyWater serves customers in quantum computing, automotive, aerospace and defense, high-performance computing and AI, industrial, and biomedical markets. Its customer base includes fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers (IDMs), original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), startups, government agencies, and research organizations. Notable partnerships include collaboration with IonQ on quantum processors and the ThermaView™ product line for advanced ROICs used in aerospace, defense, automotive, and industrial applications.

SkyWater differentiates itself through a collaborative foundry model branded as Technology-as-a-Service (TaaS), which aims to accelerate the path from concept to production. The company emphasizes secure, domestic manufacturing to support resilient supply chains and national technology leadership, and it holds DMEA accreditation as a supplier for defense applications.

Solar Renewable Energy, LLC (SRE) is based in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. The company was formed in January 2010 as a Pennsylvania limited liability corporation by Mr. Berry, drawing on his long-standing association with the public accounting firm ParenteBeard.

The company serves commercial businesses, municipalities, and not-for-profit organizations in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Ohio, the District of Columbia, Connecticut, and Delaware. It also acts as a registered PJM GATS aggregator and broker, selling tens of thousands of solar renewable energy credits each year to public utilities on behalf of its clients.

SRE emphasizes ownership structures that minimize upfront costs while delivering long-term energy savings and financial returns. Its leadership team combines project development, finance, public accounting, and taxation expertise, and the firm maintains relationships with panel, racking, inverter, and monitoring system manufacturers as well as design engineering and electrical contractor partners.

old_description: Manufactures high-power and high-voltage semiconductor products for aerospace and defense at its La Mirada, California facility.
about:
Solid State Devices, Inc. (SSDI) has operated from La Mirada, California since its founding in 1967. The company began as a supplier of hermetic semiconductor devices for critical aerospace and defense applications and has remained at that location for over five decades.

SSDI designs and manufactures high-power and high-voltage semiconductor components, including rectifiers, IGBTs, thyristors, power modules, hybrids, and assemblies. Its La Mirada facility houses wafer fabrication, assembly, and test operations, with capabilities spanning die attach, wire bonding, hermetic sealing, and a full suite of environmental and reliability screening per MIL-PRF-19500, MIL-STD-883, and related standards. The company also offers custom packaging, reverse engineering, and end-of-life solutions.

The primary customers are aerospace and defense programs, including U.S. military and space agencies. SSDI's products are qualified to JANS, the highest reliability level under MIL-PRF-19500, and the company works directly with procurement groups and design engineers on source-controlled drawings for missiles, satellites, and avionics.

SSDI emphasizes its combined 700-plus years of engineering experience drawn from alumni of firms such as Microsemi, International Rectifier, and Motorola. It maintains in-house wafer fabrication and assembly, a strong anti-counterfeit program, material lot traceability, and a willingness to accept small-quantity orders — factors the company cites as differentiators in a market often focused on high-volume production.

name: Solid State Logic
old_description: From groundbreaking audio production consoles to innovative personal studios, Solid State Logic are the world's leading manufacturer of creative tools for music, live sound and broadcast.
about:
Solid State Logic is headquartered in New York, New York, while its original manufacturing and research base remains at Begbroke Manor in Oxfordshire, UK. The company was founded in 1969 by Colin Sanders CBE, who initially developed switching systems for pipe organs before establishing Acorn Studios in the village of Stonesfield. There he built the first SSL consoles, to the SL 4000 B Series in 1976 and the breakthrough SL 4000 E Series in 1979 that transformed professional recording.

Today SSL designs and manufactures a wide range of audio hardware and software: large-format analogue and digital consoles for music, broadcast, and live sound; desktop audio interfaces; DAW controllers; 19-inch rackmount processors; 500-series modules; and an extensive library of native plug-ins. Production occurs at the 4,000-square-meter facility opened at Begbroke Manor in 1988, though current headcount and annual volumes are not disclosed.

The company serves music production studios, broadcast facilities, live-sound rental companies, post-production houses, educational institutions, installed-sound venues, touring acts, and podcast/webcast creators.

SSL differentiates itself through proprietary technologies such as SuperAnalogue™ circuitry, console-wide Instant Recall, motorised fader automation (Ultimation), and native ST 2110 IP workflows with NMOS discovery. The founder’s original drive to improve organ switching evolved into a philosophy of continuous innovation in audio signal processing and workflow integration.

For finishing, the plant operates two shrinkage-control belt dryers, 24 tumble dryers, four Fabcon compactors, a Krantz eight-bay tenter frame with a 74-inch maximum width, and a Fabcon open-width compactor. Services cover tubular and open-width fabrics, with napping and tip shearing available.

Its on-site laboratory uses Datacolor color management solutions for shade matching and conducts AATCC-standard tests for shrinkage, width, yield, stretch and recovery, torque, crocking, wash fastness, burst strength, and wicking.

The company emphasizes quality work and integrity, backed by computerized process control and a dedicated color-matching lab to meet customer color expectations reliably.
